page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7a.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7T83 processor operating at a base clock speed of 2.55 GHz, featuring 16 vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The system is provisioned with 64.0 GB of dedicated system memory, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. It includes 32 MB of L3 cache alongside instruction set extensions such as AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA_NI, but lacks bundled local ephemeral storage and GPU acceleration. Network connectivity is delivered via a baseline bandwidth of 7 Gbps.

In synthetic compute and system benchmarks, the ecs.g7a.4xlarge exhibits middle-tier performance across most evaluated metrics, achieving a Geekbench multi-core score of 8861.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 21235.7. In memory evaluation tests, cached read operations reach 1033.55 GB/sec, whereas uncached large-block operations show reduced throughput, with read bandwidth at 39.33 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 18.82 GB/sec. Application testing demonstrates strong operational throughput, including 15.73 million Redis SET operations per second, 14.72 GB/sec in static web serving, and strong small-model LLM text generation performance at 307.15 tokens per second.

The instance presents a balanced hardware profile suitable for steady general-purpose workloads, enterprise microservices, caching layers, and web application hosting. Its lack of bundled local storage requires reliance on network-attached block storage for persistent data. The combination of consistent multi-core processing capacity and high Redis throughput makes it an effective platform for backend API services, static web serving, and lightweight natural language processing tasks.

Synthetic benchmarks indicate consistent average compute capabilities, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 8861.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 21235.7. While uncached large-block memory throughput remains a limitation at 39.33 GB/sec read and 18.82 GB/sec write, cached memory performance is high at 1033.55 GB/sec. Practical application metrics reflect solid results, such as 15.73 million Redis SET operations per second, static web serving throughput of 14.72 GB/sec, and 307.15 tokens per second for small-model LLM text generation. The instance is well matched for API backend services, memory caching, microservices, and general compute workloads.
